notes: Pre-2010 morphology and Darwin-era observations document distinct stamen cohorts in M. speciosa. It is a strong species-level candidate, but the 2010 review says Malvaceae had only one reported heterantherous species whereas Spruce described similar dimorphism in multiple Mollia species; that discrepancy prevents promotion without the exact Table S1 row.

Darwin examined M. lepidota and recorded graded/differentiated stamens; Spruce described outer and inner cohorts with different filament/anther/pollen colours. This makes it a real historical alternative, not evidence that it is the representative chosen in Table S1.
Historical material reports stamen dimorphism in several Mollia species. Genus-level support is source-secure enough to narrow the search but cannot reconcile the review's one-species statement.
Retained to prevent a poricidal-anther search from drifting into a false heteranthery candidate: modern genus descriptions explicitly describe stamens as all alike.

APG III folds former Cochlospermaceae into Bixaceae. Comparative morphology places the shift from uniform stamens in Cochlospermum to dimorphic stamens in Amoreuxia, strongly narrowing the Bixaceae candidate lineage. The exact representative species used in 2010 remains unresolved.

Retained as an explicit exclusion: comparative morphology identifies Cochlospermum as the uniform-stamen side of the lineage contrast, so poricidal/buzz-pollinated Cochlospermum cannot be promoted merely from the family-level Bixaceae signal.

Verbascum is a source-supported Scrophulariaceae lineage with repeated anther/stamen dimorphism; later comparative work explicitly discusses heteranthery in Verbascum in the context of Vallejo-Marin et al. 2010. This narrows the lineage but does not identify the representative species in Table S1.
